Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome. A few quick notes before tonight's performance. The doors are going to close at seven fifty-five, five minutes before we start, so please take your seats soon. Tonight's concert is about two hours long, with a twenty-minute intermission. During the intermission, the bar on the first floor will be open. And please, turn off your phones and don't take photos while the orchestra is playing. You're very welcome to take pictures at the end, during the applause. Thank you, and enjoy the music.

My husband and I have a tradition. Once a month, we go to a concert. It doesn't matter what kind: classical, jazz, a rock band, a choir. We take turns. One month I choose, the next month he chooses. That way, we've seen things we would never choose alone. Last month it was his turn, and he took me to a heavy metal show. I was a bit scared, honestly, but the energy was amazing. Next month it's my turn, and we're going to see a jazz trio in a small club. We're meeting some friends for dinner first. I can't wait.

I've been playing the violin in this orchestra for twelve years, and I still get nervous. In the last five minutes before a concert, I don't talk to anybody. I just breathe slowly and look at the first page of the music. People think the best moment is the standing ovation. It's lovely, of course. But my favorite moment is the silence after the last note, just before the applause. For one or two seconds, nobody moves. Tonight we're playing Brahms. It's going to be a long night, but I'm sure it's going to be beautiful.
